notes: Server: the engine's 'self-hosted-server' way (native systemd service via scripts/install-pi.sh, scripts/update.sh, owner-only Update server button); Docker was used first and removed. Deliberate differences: (1) the server is built (esbuild bundle apps/server/dist/server.mjs), so update.sh runs `pnpm build`, and the installer clones with tags (the version shown comes from `git describe`); (2) the first account is the owner (lowest user id, no is_admin column) and needs a setup code the installer sets; (3) the web page needs no Cloudflare Access headers (same-origin, the browser's Access cookie covers it), but Settings > This app has an Access card that keeps the service token for the pairing code; the Android app takes an optional service token on its own address screen, used only by the widget; (4) device-pairing is taken for the Android setup screen (a KEEP1- code carries address, a token of its own and the Cloudflare Access service token); the signed-in web page still hands the widget a token through the bridge by itself; (5) Android shell differs from the engine's android-shell: it loads the SERVER's page instead of a bundled copy at http://localhost (no version skew, no CORS), applicationId app.turbokeep.android, widget + quick add + share target instead of media playback, OkHttp for native calls. Standard Notes, Vikunja and TurboKeep bundle import/export live in apps/server/src/formats and io.ts. Everything is one kind of thing, a note (schema v4): on the list (a checkbox) or filed under tags. 2026-10-18: these modules were written HERE first and ported to the engine (branch claude/turbokeep-round-5 of TurboNZL/turboengine, not merged by me): motion, local-cache, backup-bundle, custom-emoji, search-language, tag-tree, and logos' symbol-only small icons. Pin to the merged commit once that branch is in.
